summary: CODE-GATE-02: Three source-verified defects remain: one P1 branch-authority defect and two P2 stack-recovery defects. Review remained read-only; no tests, builds, paid calls, or delegation.

findings.detail: Bind local mutations to the workflow branch as well as its SHA. During the first worker invocation, switching the checkout to main at the same starting SHA passes assertExpectedHead. Git can carry the worker's edits across that switch, and commit() then commits them directly onto main. Publication eventually rejects the unchanged workflow branch, but the unauthorized local branch mutation has already occurred.
findings.evidence: assertExpectedHead checks only rev-parse HEAD at lines 122–133. commit() invokes ordinary git add and git commit on the current checkout at lines 447–460. The branch-name check exists in recovery preflight at lines 332–335, but is absent from the active work/commit boundary.

findings.detail: A recovered commit must finish its post-commit work before advancing. If an existing lower stack layer is repaired and execution stops after its commit receipt is confirmed but before descendant propagation, resume finds a clean tree and returns passed here. Descendants never receive the repair. Their subsequent reviews use the old bases, and monitoring blocks after publication because the actual parent branch SHA differs from the recorded baseHead. Further resume attempts remain in monitoring and cannot complete the omitted propagation.
findings.evidence: effect() durably confirms the new commit at lines 193–195 before commit() reaches propagateDescendants at line 477. Recovery retains resumeStage=commit, but the confirmed-receipt shortcut at lines 425–432 bypasses propagation. review() advances through existing descendants at lines 565–568; monitor() requires their recorded baseHead to equal the remote base.

findings.detail: Persist the causal unit separately from the descendant being propagated. During three-layer landing, preparing layer 2 propagates its updated head into layer 3. If execution stops after that propagation receipt is saved, the journal contains unitIndex=2 with resumeStage=prepare. Resume consequently prepares and retargets layer 3 directly to main even though layer 2 has not landed. It also skips layer 2's invalidated checks and reviews, so publication then blocks on missing evidence.
findings.evidence: propagateDescendants changes run.unitIndex at line 488, and effect() persists the whole run before and after the merge. Restoring the index at line 507 is not itself persisted. preflight returns the saved prepare stage at lines 355–358; prepare() uses current(run) and retargets it at lines 838–845 without checking that its predecessor merged.
